newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's El-Op acquires Terra computer maker.
newsitem.headline: Israel's El-Op acquires Terra computer maker.

text.p: Israel's El-Op Electro-optic Industries Ltd said on Monday it had acquired for an undisclosed sum 60 percent of Terra Computers Ltd, an Israeli maker of specialised personal computers.
"The acquisition is part of El-Op's policy of moving into the civilian market," Chaim Russo, El-Op's deputy managing director for business and technology development, told Reuters.

Terra, a start-up company, develops, manufactures and markets computers for specialised niche applications. Its TR-2000 is designed for use in financial modelling, computer animation, machine simulation and weather forecasting.
Russo said El-Op hoped to float Terra in the United States before the end of 1997.
He said Terra began sales in 1996 and they will amount to just a few hundreds of thousands of dollars for the full year. Among its customers is the U.S. National Institutes of Health.

Russo said the purchase was part of El-Op's long-term strategy to diversify out of the defence-electronics sector. The privately-held company makes thermal-imaging systems, lasers, range finders and fire control systems for military use.

El-Op enjoyed an upsurge in sales after the 1991 Gulf War, where many of the technologies El-Op employs were proven in the battlefield. But, Russo said, "because of the (long-term) problems in this market, we want to diversify."
He said El-Op, which will have sales this year of $270 million, aims to derive 20 percent of its sales from civilian products.
Terra marks its first acquisition, but Russo said the company had formed subsidiaries to develop civilian products in areas such as machine vision.
